clue.text: Game served with two cuts of bacon

parts.note: back bacon is a cut taken from the pig's loin
gammon is a cut from the pig's hind leg, cured like bacon

explanation.surface: A diner is brought a meal accompanied by a couple of rashers.
explanation.walkthrough: The one phrase supplies both pieces: two British cuts of bacon, back and gammon, set side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A board game for two players, moving counters round a board by throws of dice.

clue.text: Bankrupt after buying a sculpture

explanation.surface: Someone goes broke after spending on a piece of art.
explanation.definitionFit: Broke or ruined is one slang sense; a carved head and shoulders is the other, a type of statue.

clue.text: Cut roast meat in extortionate nightclub

parts.note: to clip is to cut or trim
a joint is a large piece of meat for roasting

explanation.surface: Someone trims a roast inside an overpriced club.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a bar or club that overcharges or swindles its customers.

clue.text: Youth leader holds up fool from ditch

indicators.note: in a down answer the piece written below supports the one above, so this places it last

parts.note: to gull is to fool, and a gull is a dupe

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A youth club leader delays a fool emerging from a ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'holds up' means the Y sits beneath GULL, propping it up.
explanation.definitionFit: A gully is a channel or narrow ravine cut by water, much like a ditch.

clue.text: Fail to meet one on diplomatic duty

parts.note: to miss someone is to fail to meet them
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone misses an appointment with an envoy who is on an official posting.
explanation.definitionFit: A posting abroad on official business, as in a trade or diplomatic delegation.

clue.text: Earl's so distressed when unable to row

indicators.note: distressed means agitated or damaged, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A nobleman is upset because he cannot row his boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distressed' rearranges the letters of EARL'S SO, the apostrophe ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Without any blades to propel a boat, so a rower would be helpless.

clue.text: Effrontery from foul-mouthed expert

indicators.note: the mouth of the word foul is taken as its opening letter

parts.note: an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: Cheek coming from a specialist who swears a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foul-mouthed' is read as the mouth, or front, of 'foul', giving F.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve or cheek, as in having the gall to do something.

clue.text: A lovely French and English tree

parts.note: bel is a French word for beautiful or lovely

explanation.surface: A handsome tree that is both French and English.
explanation.definitionFit: The white poplar, a tall tree with silvery leaves.

clue.text: Former location of trade-fair

parts.note: ex is a prefix meaning former
a position is a location

explanation.surface: The site where a trade show once took place.
explanation.definitionFit: A large public show of goods or industry, like the Great Exhibition.

clue.text: Head swineherd intends to get swine's food

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: will means intends, as in 'I will go'

explanation.surface: The chief pig-keeper plans to feed the pigs.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitchen scraps mixed with liquid, fed to pigs.

clue.text: Ideal place to discard dilapidated motor

definitions.text: Ideal place to discard dilapidated motor

parts.words: Ideal place to discard dilapidated motor
parts.note: an old banger of a car is a heap, and the spot for junk is where it belongs, a place for unwanted rubbish

explanation.surface: Where to dump a worn-out car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heap' is slang for an old car, so the answer neatly names the place for one.
explanation.definitionFit: A pile of discarded metal and junk, where useless things end up.

clue.text: Hang it, that's his job!

parts.note: 'Hang it!' looks like an exasperated oath, but 'it' is wallpaper, and hanging it is a decorator's trade

explanation.surface: An exasperated exclamation about someone's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hang it!' reads as a mild curse; literally it is what a decorator does with wallpaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorator who hangs wallpaper for a living.

clue.text: Pleasure trip may result in prosecution

definitions.text: Pleasure trip may result in prosecution

parts.words: Pleasure trip may result in prosecution
parts.note: an outing for fun in a car taken without the owner's consent, an offence that lands thieves in court

explanation.surface: A jaunt for enjoyment that ends up in court.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the word is used for driving a stolen car for kicks, a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: A reckless ride in a stolen vehicle, done for thrills.

clue.text: Backstop heartened by English linesmen

indicators.note: given a new heart, so the letter is placed in the middle of the turned word
the front of the word Backstop tells us to read stop backwards

explanation.surface: A baseball catcher is encouraged by English line judges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reverses STOP to POTS, and 'heartened by' puts E in its middle. Linesmen are writers of verse lines, not sports officials.
explanation.definitionFit: Writers of verse, who compose in lines.

clue.text: Carol carries jumble and gets direly hot

indicators.note: one word carries the other, holding it within

parts.note: to carol is to sing
a welter is a confused jumble

explanation.surface: A carol singer hauls a mess and becomes terribly overheated.
explanation.definitionFit: Oppressively and uncomfortably warm, as on a stifling day.

clue.text: What boxers do before they join the fray

explanation.surface: The routine of boxers ahead of a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase works twice: the pre-fight ritual on scales, and joining a fray in the sense of entering a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: Fighters stepping on the scales ahead of a bout is one sense; entering an argument or fight is the other.

clue.text: Reactionary bowler, perhaps

explanation.surface: A right-wing cricketer, it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: A conservative diehard is one sense; a stiff helmet-like headgear, of which a bowler is an example, is the other.

clue.text: Taverns need tidying up daily

indicators.note: tidying up rearranges things, so the letters of the word Taverns are reordered

explanation.surface: Pubs must be cleaned every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daily' is a noun here: in Britain a daily is a cleaner who comes in each day.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic help, someone employed to clean.

clue.text: A Catholic man — kind, yet original

parts.note: RC stands for Roman Catholic
he is a man
a type is a kind

explanation.surface: A Catholic man who is kind yet inventive.
explanation.definitionFit: A prototype or perfect model from which copies derive.

clue.text: Hindrance to doctor before operation, it's hinted

indicators.note: before places the doctor ahead of the operation in the answer

parts.note: a let is a hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: Something obstructs a doctor ahead of surgery, so it is rumoured.
explanation.definitionFit: To mention casually or reveal by accident, as a hint.

clue.text: Arctic feline is a foul-smelling animal

parts.note: the Arctic lies about the North Pole
a feline is a cat

explanation.surface: A snow cat is a stinky creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark-furred weasel relative known for its strong odour.

clue.text: Dire blow for knight confronting two army chiefs

indicators.note: confronting means facing, so the knight stands in front of the chiefs

parts.note: Sir is a knight's title
OC stands for officer commanding
CO stands for commanding officer

explanation.surface: A grim blow for a knight facing two generals.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot, oppressive wind blowing from Africa into southern Europe.

clue.text: Trainee tucked in to hot German bread

indicators.note: tucked in to means placed inside another word

parts.note: hot is slang for stolen
L, from learner plates, means a trainee

explanation.surface: A trainee scoffs warm German loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruit loaf with marzipan, eaten at Christmas.

clue.text: Age old church record found first

indicators.note: the record is found at the front of the answer

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: An ancient church register turns up at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A long period of history, an era.

clue.text: Done to a t, that's evident

parts.note: over means finished or done

explanation.surface: Perfectly cooked, that is plain to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Done to a t' suggests perfection, but read literally it gives the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Open and plainly visible, not hidden.

clue.text: Acclaim British rugby team for including one oriental

indicators.note: including means holding within, so one letter is set inside the team

parts.note: the British and Irish Lions are a touring rugby side
I is the Roman numeral for one
E for East, i.e. oriental

explanation.surface: Praise the British rugby side for signing an Asian player.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat someone as a celebrity, praising them lavishly.

clue.text: Is allowed to give an inch

parts.note: let means allowed

explanation.surface: Permission to yield a small amount.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scotland an inch is a small island, so 'an inch' is not a measurement.
explanation.definitionFit: A small island, which Scots call an inch.

clue.text: Detect epidermic eruption

explanation.surface: Notice a breakout on the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: To notice or see is one sense; a pimple is the other.

clue.text: Exactly like dialect in process of change

indicators.note: a process of change implies the letters are being reordered

explanation.surface: Precisely like a dialect that is changing.
explanation.definitionFit: The same in every detail.

clue.text: Put out of commission in store

explanation.surface: Lay aside equipment in storage.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a ship or car out of service is one sense; to keep for future use is the other.

clue.text: Getting essential data takes nerve

explanation.surface: Retrieving key information demands courage.
explanation.definitionFit: The core of a matter is one sense; courage is the other.

clue.text: Rise to negotiate and pick up the tab

parts.note: to stand is to rise
to treat is to negotiate, as with an enemy

explanation.surface: Get up to bargain and then pay the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay for everyone, settling the bill.
